To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plasma levels of miR-21, miR-494 (and miR-1972) are higher in patients with classical Hodgkin lymphomas than controls and return to normal at remissions.

(1) microRNA (miRNA) biomarkers can be identified in plasma from patients with cHL; (2) miRNA levels are elevated in patients with cHl compared with healthy donors; and (3) miRNA levels decrease to normal levels in patients who achieve remission, and this change in levels reflects interim therapy response.
plasma microRNA levels reflect interim disease response in classical Hodgkin lymphomas and are therefore potential biomarkers for this cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and validation of novel disease response biomarkers for classical HL (cHL).
understanding how the microenvironment of cHL tumors influences the biology and treatment response of the malignant HRS cells.
the role of microRNAs in classical Hodgkin lymphomas (cHL) and their potential as biomarkers of disease response in patients with cHl.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
plasma levels of miR-21, miR-155, miR-494 or miR-1972 are not useful for the diagnosis of cHL or the prediction of treatment response in cHL.
miR-494 can be used as a diagnostic marker in cHL.
miR-494 can serve as a disease response biomarker in classical Hodgkin lymphomas (cHL), but that the other miRNAs tested (miR-21, miR-155, and miR1973) are not suitable as disease response biomarker.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
circulating cell-free microRNA can be used as a disease response biomarker in cHL.
we have shown that circulating microRNAs can reflect response to treatment in patients with classical Hodgkin lymphomas and that this may have clinical relevance in the management of these patients.
circulating miRNAs are potential biomarkers for disease response in classical Hodgkin lymphomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a panel of circulating miRNAs that can be used to assess disease response in patients with cHl.
